newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil talks restart after natgas deal.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil talks restart after natgas deal.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union will resume collective contract talks with state-run oil company Ecopetrol Thursday afternoon, union leader Hernando Hernandez said.

The move, dispelling fears of a possible sector-wide strike, follows a late-night breakthrough Wednesday in negotiations over the creation of a new company to handle natural gas distribution, to be called Ecogas.
The 7,000-strong USO union and Ecogas had been deadlocked over the issue of whether Ecogas should be fully independent or remain as a subsidiary of Ecogas.

But in a complex compromise solution, still to be approved by Congress, both sides agreed that Ecogas would be set up as an independent, autonomous, state-owned company within a holding group headed by Ecopetrol.

Hernandez said this would effectively mean that Ecogas would have complete independence in day-to-day decision-making but that Ecopetrol would take a central role in long-term development plans. An Ecopetrol spokesman said the compromise effectively meant that the relationship between Ecopetrol and Ecogas would be "operational and commercial".
The accord also provided guarantees to prevent the eventual privatization of Ecogas or the creation of a mixed capital company through the sale of shares.
"This agreement will help Colombians in general. The accord interprets the needs of the government and Congress and also the interests of the workers," Hernandez told Reuters.
"There will be a close relationship between Ecopetrol and Ecogas although Ecogas will be an autonomous state company," he added.
The issue of Ecogas had become one of the major sticking points in collective contracts talks, which have been bogged down since early January.

The main question still to be resolved, Hernandez said, is that of salary hikes. The government has offered a basic 18 percent plus a productivity benefit, which would push the total raise to about 21 percent, the Ecopetrol spokesman said. The USO union has cut its initial demand of 30 percent to 28 percent but Hernandez said there was further margin for flexibility.
